description: Phase B definition-of-done gap (2026-08-19): cluster parameters and policies currently live in coordinator raft state (authoritative - recovery reads context.cluster_config from it) AND are written to the keyspace every recovery (cluster/parameters/*, cluster/policies/*, config_monolithic) where they are never read back - a write-only shadow copy that could silently diverge. FDB's model: \xff/conf is authoritative; coordinators hold only the connection string (../foundationdb fdbclient/ManagementAPI, coordinators only store cluster file). Target: the keyspace copies become authoritative (read back at recovery via the metadata shard, changed via ordinary transactions), and coordinator raft shrinks to the bootstrap anchor (epoch, log identities per bedrock-aum, coordinator membership). The legacy config_monolithic/epoch_legacy/last_recovery_legacy family is deleted once nothing consumes it. Sequencing: after q67.9's read path exists (recovery must be able to read config from the keyspace before raft stops carrying it).

comments.text: Audit 2026-08-20: this ticket's premise changed under it. q67.31 DELETED the write-only shadow copy - cluster/parameters/*, cluster/policies/*, and the config_monolithic/epoch_legacy/last_recovery_legacy family are no longer written at all (and their codecs are gone from SystemKeys.Values). There is no divergence hazard anymore; coordinator raft is cleanly the sole authority. The ticket's shape flips from 'promote the existing keyspace copy to authoritative' to 'introduce the keyspace config family WITH its recovery-time reader in one move' (per the inventory-not-communication rule: the writer lands with the reader, shaped by the reader). The legacy-family deletion listed as cleanup here is already done. Sequencing unchanged: after q67.9's read path.

Additional scope from the 2026-08-20 census: (1) replication_factor is re-derived as max(1, map_size(logs)) in two sites (topology snapshot, streaming) while cluster config carries desired_replication_factor unread - config authority should make the keyspace copy the single source. (2) The object-storage bootstrap dual-writes log ids (persistence_phase writes; coordinator cold-boot reads for quorum planning) - the same fact as layout/logs/. The bootstrap stays the cold-boot anchor (coordinated-state analogue), but decide the anchor's MINIMUM contents here. (3) Boundary statement to document: the coordinator raft service directory is pre-recovery discovery input ONLY (FDB CC-registration analogue, also not keyspace); nothing steady-state may read it.

Draft PR: https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/pull/266 — desired_commit_proxies moved to \xff/system/config/ with its reader (materializer bootstrap reads the family at the recovery version; commit-proxy startup consumes it; persistence seeds it once). Coordinator bootstrap keeps it as the anchor only. Remaining parameters/policies + census items filed as bedrock-q67.50; the missing operator-facing config writer as bedrock-q67.51. Stacked on #251.

title: Cluster config authority: keyspace owns parameters/policies; coordinator keeps only the bootstrap anchor
